## §3 Discovery

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `discovery.well-known` A Company publishes its `poppy.json` document at `https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json` over HTTPS, where `{domain}` is the Company's domain or a subdomain it controls. [↗](pap-0.1/03-discovery.md#L9) | MUST | company | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| – | `discovery.redirect` The well-known URL may redirect to where the document is hosted, and the document still speaks for the domain the Personal Agent requested. [↗](pap-0.1/03-discovery.md#L10) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `discovery.redirect-https` Personal Agents follow redirects, and every redirect is to an HTTPS URL. [↗](pap-0.1/03-discovery.md#L11) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.cache` Personal Agents cache the document according to its HTTP caching headers. [↗](pap-0.1/03-discovery.md#L12) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `identity.client-id-url` A Personal Agent's `client_id` is an HTTPS URL that returns its client metadata document. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L33) | MUST | both | `identity/client-id-is-url` |

| ✓ | `identity.same-domain` `jwks_uri` and every entry in `redirect_uris` are HTTPS URLs on the same domain as `client_id`, and the key set contains only public keys. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L35) | MUST | both | `identity/keys-same-domain` |
| ✓ | `identity.private-key-jwt` The Personal Agent authenticates at the token endpoint with a client assertion signed by a key from `jwks_uri` (`private_key_jwt`, RFC 7523); its DPoP keys are separate and unpublished. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L36) | MUST | both | `identity/client-auth-required`<br>`identity/client-assertion-claims`<br>`identity/client-assertion-replay` |

| – | `identity.allow-block` Companies may keep allowlists or blocklists of Personal Agents by `client_id`, and may revoke a `client_id` that misuses the protocol. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L39) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `identity.rate-limit` Companies may rate-limit Session creation by `client_id`. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L40) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `identity.new-client-limit` A Company that doesn't require registration may limit how many new `client_id` values it accepts. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L41) | MAY | company |  |

## §4.2 Starting a Session

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `sessions.user-id-stable` The Personal Agent gives each of its Users a stable User ID for each Company, where a Company is identified by its `auth.issuer`. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L58) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.user-id-no-pii` A User ID does not contain or derive from personal information, such as an email address, phone number or name, even with a keyed hash. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L59) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `sessions.jwt-bearer` A Session starts with the JWT bearer grant at `token_endpoint`: a short-lived assertion signed with a key from `jwks_uri`, with `iss` the `client_id`, `sub` the User ID, `aud` the `token_endpoint` as a single string, `iat`, `exp`, and a `jti` of at least 128 random bits, plus the client assertion and a DPoP Proof. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L60) | MUST | both | `sessions/start-signed-out`<br>`dpop/required` |
| ✓ | `sessions.verify-assertions` The Company verifies both assertions against the Personal Agent's `jwks_uri`, checks that the assertion's `iss` is the authenticated `client_id`, and rejects a reused `jti`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L61) | MUST | company | `identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| ✓ | `sessions.response` The token response carries `access_token`, `token_type` (`DPoP`, or `Bearer` for a request without a proof), `expires_in`, `scope` (empty when signed out), `session_id` and `signed_in`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L62) | MUST | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.expires-in` `expires_in` is greater than 0. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L63) | MUST | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.token-hours` Session Tokens last hours, not days. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L64) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.renew-same-owner` On renewal with `session_id`, the Company checks that the Session belongs to the same `client_id` and User ID as the assertion, and returns `invalid_session` if the Session has ended or belongs to someone else. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L65) | MUST | company | `sessions/renew-same-owner` |
| → | `sessions.opaque-tokens` Personal Agents do not depend on the contents of Session Tokens. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L66) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `sessions.embedded-credentials` A Company may include its own Session credentials in a token so its existing systems can read them. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L67) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `sessions.embedded-encrypted` A Company that includes its own Session credentials in a token encrypts the token. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L68) | MUST | company | `sessions/token-opaque` |
| ✓ | `sessions.errors` Token endpoint errors use the OAuth error response: `invalid_client` 401, `invalid_grant` 400, `invalid_session` 400, `account_mismatch` 400, `invalid_dpop_proof` and `use_dpop_nonce` 400, `rate_limited` 429 with `Retry-After`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L69) | MUST | company | `sessions/renew-same-owner`<br>`dpop/required` |

## §4.3 Using Session Tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tokens.dpop-scheme` API calls and conversations carry the Session Token in the `Authorization` header with the `DPoP` scheme, together with a DPoP Proof. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L78) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `dpop.key-per-session` The Personal Agent generates a key pair for each User at each Company, and may use a new one for each Session. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L79) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `dpop.proof-claims` A proof has `jti`, `htm` and `htu` (the request's method and URL without the query or fragment), `iat`, `ath` (the SHA-256 hash of the Session Token, absent at the token endpoint), and `nonce` when required. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L80) | MUST | both | `dpop/htu` |
| ✓ | `dpop.bind` When the Company issues a Session Token, it binds the token to the key in that request's proof. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L81) | MUST | company | `dpop/api-binding` |
| ✓ | `dpop.verify` On every request the Company checks that the proof's signature verifies with the key in its header, that the key is the one the Session Token is bound to, that `htm` and `htu` match the request, that `iat` is within its acceptance window, that it hasn't accepted the same `jti` within that window, and that `ath` matches the Session Token. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L82) | MUST | company | `dpop/replay`<br>`dpop/htu`<br>`dpop/htm`<br>`dpop/iat-window`<br>`dpop/signature`<br>`dpop/jti-entropy`<br>`dpop/api-binding` |
| – | `dpop.nonce` A Company may require proofs to include a nonce it issued. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L83) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `dpop.nonce-support` Personal Agents support DPoP nonces. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L84) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `dpop.errors` Failed proof checks return `invalid_dpop_proof` or `use_dpop_nonce` with the `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` header. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L85) | MUST | company | `dpop/required` |
| ✓ | `tokens.mcp-bearer` For MCP, the Personal Agent requests a Session Token without a proof and with `resource` set to the MCP server's `url` from `poppy.json`, and the Company issues a `Bearer` token that works at only that MCP server. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L86) | MUST | both | `mcp/bearer-token` |
| ✓ | `tokens.bearer-only-mcp` Companies accept Bearer Session Tokens only on their MCP APIs, and require DPoP everywhere else. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L87) | MUST | company | `mcp/resource-bound`<br>`tokens/dpop-outside-mcp` |
| → | `tokens.narrower` Any token request may include `scope`, to ask for fewer scopes than the Session has, and `resource` (RFC 8707), to ask for a token for one service. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L88) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.resource-bound` A service whose `poppy.json` entry has a `resource` accepts a token only if it was issued for that `resource`; otherwise one DPoP Session Token works at all of a Company's services except MCP. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L89) | MUST | company | `tokens/dpop-outside-mcp` |
| ✓ | `tokens.no-cookies` Companies accept the token in the `Authorization` header without requiring cookies. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L90) | MUST | company | `mcp/protocol`<br>`apis/openapi` |
| → | `tokens.always-send` Personal Agents send a Session Token on every API and conversation request, and never leave it out to appear to the Company as a person. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L91) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.use-newest` Whenever the Personal Agent gets a new Session Token for a Session, it uses the new token from then on. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L92) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.not-in-url` Personal Agents do not send tokens in a URL, and Companies do not accept them from one. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L93) | MUST NOT | both | `mcp/token-not-in-url` |
| ✓ | `tokens.rate-limit` A Company that limits request rates returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header when a request goes over the limit, on any endpoint, API, conversation or website. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L94) | MUST | company | `mediated/rate-limit`<br>`tokens/rate-limit` |
| → | `tokens.retry-after` On HTTP 429 the Personal Agent waits at least the `Retry-After` time before sending the request again. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sessions.md#L95) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.5 Direct Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `direct.consent` The Company's page shows which Personal Agent is asking, with the name and logo from its metadata, and the requested scopes, and lets the User approve some or all of them, or decline. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L35) | MUST | company | `direct/consent-page`<br>`signin/partial-approval` |

| ✓ | `direct.redirect-exact` `redirect_uri` exactly matches an entry in the Personal Agent's `redirect_uris`. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L37) | MUST | company | `direct/redirect-exact` |
| → | `direct.iss-check` The Personal Agent checks `state`, and checks that `iss` exactly matches the `auth.issuer` of the Company it started sign-in with. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L38) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

| → | `account.narrow` `scope` may ask for fewer scopes than the Account Token has. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L73) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `account.no-widen` A refresh can't ask for more scopes than the Account Token has. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L74) | MUST NOT | company | `account/no-widen` |
| ✓ | `account.lifetime` Using an Account Token doesn't extend its lifetime, and an expired or revoked one returns `invalid_grant` while the Session continues signed out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L75) | MUST | company | `account/refresh`<br>`signout/revoke` |
| – | `account.rotation` A Company may return a new Account Token in `refresh_token`. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L76) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `account.use-rotated` When the Company returns a new Account Token, the Personal Agent uses the new one from then on. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L77) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `account.secret` Personal Agents store Account Tokens as secrets, and never put them in model context, conversation messages, logs or URLs. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L78) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.9 Signing out

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `signout.revoke` The Company revokes the Account Token and signs out every Session signed in with it, and those Sessions continue signed out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L84) | MUST | company | `signout/revoke` |
| – | `signout.end-sessions` A Company may end the Sessions at sign-out instead, and renewal then returns `invalid_session`. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L85) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `signout.check-per-request` Companies check on each request whether the Session is still signed in, so sign-out takes effect right away. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L86) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/ended-session`<br>`signout/revoke`<br>`web/follows-session` |
| ✎ | `signout.short-lifetimes` A Company that doesn't check sign-in on each request uses much shorter Session Token lifetimes, such as a few minutes. [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L87) | SHOULD | company | _Poppyseed checks the Session on every request, so the alternative does not apply_ |
| ✓ | `signout.disconnect` When the User disconnects the Personal Agent in account settings, the Company revokes its Account Tokens for that account and signs out its Sessions. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/04-sign-in.md#L88) | MUST | company | `signout/disconnect` |

## §5 Web browsing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `web.join-before-browse` When a Company lists `web.browser_session_endpoint`, the Personal Agent joins its browser to a Session before browsing the Company's website. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L18) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `web.assertion` The browser assertion is a JWT signed with a key from the Personal Agent's `jwks_uri`, with `typ` `poppy-browser+jwt`, `aud` the endpoint, the `session_id` to join, `return_to`, and `exp` no more than 60 seconds after `iat`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L19) | MUST | both | `web/join` |
| ✓ | `web.return-to` `return_to` is an HTTPS URL on the Company's `organization.domain` or one of its subdomains. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L20) | MUST | both | `web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.assertion-in-body` The browser posts the assertion as a form POST in a top-level navigation, in the request body, never in the URL. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L21) | MUST | both | `web/join` |
| → | `web.agent-browser` The Personal Agent posts browser assertions only from a browser it controls, never from the User's own browser. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `web.verify-assertion` The Company checks the signature against the `iss` client's `jwks_uri` and that `typ` is `poppy-browser+jwt`, that `aud` is its endpoint and the assertion hasn't expired with `exp` at most 60 seconds after `iat`, that it hasn't accepted the `jti` before, that the Session is active and belongs to the same `client_id` and User, and that `return_to` is on its own domain. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L23) | MUST | company | `web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.assertion-types` A Session assertion isn't accepted at the browser session endpoint, and a browser assertion isn't accepted at the token endpoint. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L24) | MUST | company | `web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.response` When every check passes, the Company sets a cookie for the Session and responds `303 See Other` to `return_to`; otherwise it sets no cookie and returns an error page with HTTP 400. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L25) | MUST | company | `web/join`<br>`web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-follows-session` The cookie follows the Session's current state, so when the Session signs in or out or its scopes change, the website reflects it on the next request. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L26) | MUST | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-lifetime` The cookie does not outlive the Session. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L27) | MUST NOT | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-flags` The cookie is `Secure` and `HttpOnly`, and uses `SameSite=Lax` or `None`, not `Strict`. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L28) | MUST | company | `web/join` |
| ✓ | `web.scopes` The website applies the Session's scopes, and while the browser carries the Session's cookie the Company handles its requests as that Session, whatever other cookies the browser holds. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L29) | MUST | company | `web/follows-session` |
| → | `web.rejoin` The Personal Agent may post a new browser assertion at any time, and each one replaces the cookie the Company set before. [↗](pap-0.1/05-web.md#L30) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 APIs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `apis.types` Each API's `type` is `openapi` or `mcp`. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L20) | MUST | company | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| ✓ | `apis.openapi-description` An `openapi` entry's `url` points to an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 description of the API. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L21) | MUST | company | `apis/openapi` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-transport` An `mcp` entry's `url` is a remote MCP server endpoint using the Streamable HTTP transport and MCP version 2025-06-18 or later. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L22) | MUST | company | `mcp/protocol` |
| → | `apis.skip-unknown` Personal Agents skip API types they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L23) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `apis.session-tokens` Every listed API accepts Session Tokens as described in 4.3: DPoP for OpenAPI, and Bearer for MCP. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L24) | MUST | company | `apis/openapi` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-scopes` A listed MCP server accepts Session Tokens as its access tokens and enforces their scopes. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L25) | MUST | company | `mcp/public-tool`<br>`mcp/scope-challenge` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-resource` A listed MCP server accepts only tokens issued for its `url`. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L26) | MUST | company | `mcp/resource-bound` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-metadata` The MCP server's protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) lists `auth.issuer` in `authorization_servers`. [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L27) | MUST | company | `mcp/challenge` |
| ✓ | `apis.errors` Token failures at APIs return `invalid_token` (401), `sign_in_required` (403) or `insufficient_scope` (403, naming the scopes in `scope`) in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/06-apis.md#L28) | MUST | company | `mcp/challenge`<br>`mcp/scope-challenge` |

## §7.1 Conversation protocols

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.protocol-choice` The Personal Agent chooses a protocol it supports from `agent.protocols`, uses that entry's endpoint, and skips unfamiliar types. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L9) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.2 Requests

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.session-token` Every conversation request carries a Session Token with a DPoP Proof. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L21) | MUST | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.isolation` A conversation belongs to the `client_id` and User ID that started it, and to the account once it uses one; the Company rejects requests from any other `client_id`, User or account. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L22) | MUST | company | `conv/isolation`<br>`conv/account-bound` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-format` Conversation, message and event IDs are strings of 1 to 256 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L23) | MUST | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-prefix` IDs start with a short prefix for their kind, such as `cnv_`, `msg_` or `evt_`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L24) | SHOULD | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-opaque` Beyond the format rules, the side that doesn't choose an ID does not depend on its format. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L25) | MUST NOT | both | `conv/start` |

## §7.3 Sending messages

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.start` Starting a conversation returns HTTP 201 with `conversation_id`, `status` and `responder`, and later messages to `{id}/messages` return HTTP 202 with the same fields. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L29) | MUST | company | `conv/start` |
| → | `conv.message-id-unique` The Personal Agent makes each message `id` unique for the User, and retries a message with the same ID. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L30) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.message-idempotent` A message with an already accepted ID and the same content returns the original response without adding it again, including a retried first message; different content returns `message_id_conflict`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L31) | MUST | company | `conv/message-idempotent` |
| ✓ | `conv.wait` With `wait` (and optionally `cursor`) on either POST, the Company accepts the message, then responds as a read of the events from that cursor would, holding the request up to `wait` seconds, with status 201 or 202. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L32) | MUST | company | `conv/reply` |

## §7.4 Message fields

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.message-content` A message has at least one of `text`, `data` or `context`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L44) | MUST | both | `conv/message-content` |
| ✓ | `conv.text-plain` Personal Agents and Company Agents do not put JSON or other markup in `text`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L45) | SHOULD NOT | both | `conv/reply` |
| → | `conv.context-formats` When the Personal Agent shares `locale`, `time_zone` or `user_available`, it uses those fields and their formats: an RFC 5646 language tag, an IANA time zone name, and a boolean. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L46) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conv.context-extra` `context` may include other fields. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L47) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `conv.context-ignore` A Company may ignore `context` fields beyond those defined. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L48) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conv.context-minimal` Personal Agents share only what the task needs. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L49) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.context-sticky` `context` fields a message leaves out keep their previous values, and only the Personal Agent sends `context`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L50) | MUST | company | `conv/context-sticky` |

## §7.5 Reading events

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.skip-unknown-events` Personal Agents skip event types they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L56) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conv.cursor-opaque` Cursors are opaque, and the Personal Agent does not compare or sort them. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L57) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.events` Each event's `id` is also a cursor, a read without `cursor` starts at the beginning, and a read that times out returns an empty `events` list. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L58) | MUST | company | `conv/start`<br>`conv/cursors` |
| – | `conv.wait-cap` The Company may return a read before `wait` elapses, or cap `wait`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L59) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `conv.read-fields` Every successful read includes `cursor`, `has_more`, `status` and `responder`, even with no events; `cursor` is the last event returned, or the request's cursor if there were none. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L60) | MUST | company | `conv/start`<br>`conv/cursors` |
| ✓ | `conv.cursor-expired-error` A cursor for events the Company no longer has returns `cursor_expired`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L61) | MUST | company | `conv/cursor-expired` |
| → | `conv.cursor-expired` On `cursor_expired` the Personal Agent reads from the beginning and tells the User that part of the conversation is missing. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L62) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.6 Streaming

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conv.sse` A Company may stream events with server-sent events when a read sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, with each event's ID as the SSE `id` and the event JSON as `data`; one that doesn't stream returns JSON. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L66) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `conv.sse-close` A Company may close a stream at any time, and the Personal Agent reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L67) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `conv.text-delta` While the Company Agent writes a message, the Company may send pieces of its text as `text-delta` events with no SSE `id`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L68) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conv.text-delta-ignore` The Personal Agent does not act on text from a `text-delta` event. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L69) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.7 Status and responder

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.status-responder` Every successful response to a POST or a read includes `status` and `responder`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L75) | MUST | company | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.state-events` Every change to `status` or `responder` adds a `state` event with both. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L76) | MUST | company | `conv/reply`<br>`conv/handoff` |
| ✓ | `conv.company-sender` Each Company message includes `sender`, `agent` or `human`, and its `role` stays `company`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L77) | MUST | company | `conv/reply`<br>`conv/handoff` |

## §7.8 Human or AI

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.agent-sender` The Personal Agent sets each message's `sender` to `agent` when it wrote the message, and to `human` only when the message carries the User's own words. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L81) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.9 Handoff to a person

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.handoff` A handoff request with an empty JSON object returns HTTP 202 with `status` and `responder`; the status becomes `queued`, `responder` becomes `human` when a person joins, and if no one is available the status returns to `idle` with a message saying why. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L85) | MUST | company | `conv/handoff` |

## §7.10 Direct Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.direct` The parent of a Direct Conversation is open, belongs to the same owner, is not itself a Direct Conversation, and has at most one open Direct Conversation; otherwise the Company returns `conversation_not_found`, `conversation_closed` or `direct_conversation_open`. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L89) | MUST | company | `conv/direct` |
| ✓ | `conv.direct-parent` Opening and closing a Direct Conversation adds `direct_opened` and `direct_closed` events to the parent, the parent refuses messages and handoff with `direct_conversation_open` while it is open, and closing the parent closes its open Direct Conversation. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L90) | MUST | company | `conv/direct` |

## §7.11 Sign-in during a conversation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.authorization-message` When the Company adds an `authorization` event, it also asks in a message. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L94) | SHOULD | company | `conv/sign-in` |
| → | `conv.token-switch` The Personal Agent may switch to a new Session Token partway through a conversation, or continue it in a new Session, as long as the token matches the conversation's owner. [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L95) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.scopes` Before reading account information or making a change, the Company Agent checks for the required scopes, whoever is handling the conversation, and sending a message does not authorize an account action. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L96) | MUST | company | `conv/scopes` |
| ✓ | `conv.account-bound` Once a conversation has used the User's account, a request on it from a token that isn't signed in to that account gets `sign_in_required`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L97) | MUST | company | `conv/account-bound` |

## §7.12 Closing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.close` Closing with an empty JSON object adds a `state` event with `status: "closed"`, cancels any pending handoff and returns HTTP 200; a closed conversation takes no more messages and its events stay readable. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L101) | MUST | company | `conv/close`<br>`conv/handoff` |

## §7.13 Errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.errors` Non-token errors have a JSON body with an `error` code and the statuses above, and an unknown Conversation ID and one belonging to someone else return the same `conversation_not_found`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/07-conversations.md#L114) | MUST | company | `conv/message-idempotent`<br>`conv/cursors`<br>`conv/isolation`<br>`conv/close` |

## Operations 3 Operations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `ops.id` `operation_id` may be the ID of the Company's own record for the action. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L19) | MAY | company |  |

[↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L20) | MUST | company | _the summary and terms are written by the Company's own handlers_ |
| ✓ | `ops.perform-confirmed-only` The Company performs only what the confirmed revision describes. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L21) | MUST | company | `ops/performs` |

| ✓ | `ops.final-immutable` A final operation never changes state again, and a new attempt gets a new proposal with a new operation ID. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L23) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm`<br>`ops/unknown-outcome` |

## Operations 3.1 Revisions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.frozen-revisions` The Company does not change the terms of a revision once issued, only the latest revision can be confirmed, and after confirmation the terms can't change. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L27) | MUST NOT | company | `ops/revisions` |

## Operations 3.2 Who can use an operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.access` An operation belongs to the Session it was proposed in and, if that Session is signed in, to the account, and the Company returns `operation_not_found` to anyone else. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L31) | MUST | company | `ops/access` |
| ✓ | `ops.readable` The Company keeps an operation readable at least until it is final. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L32) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm`<br>`ops/in-progress` |

## Operations 4 Proposing an operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.dedupe` If the same action comes up again through another channel, the Company returns the existing operation instead of proposing a new one. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L36) | SHOULD | company | `ops/dedupe` |
| ✓ | `ops.channels` An OpenAPI endpoint returns HTTP 202 with the operation in `operation`, an MCP tool returns it in `structuredContent.operation` with the summary as text, and a Company message carries it in `operation`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L37) | MUST | company | `ops/propose`<br>`conv/operation-message` |
| ✓ | `ops.openapi-marker` The Company says in its OpenAPI description which endpoints return operations. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L38) | SHOULD | company | `ops/advertised` |
| ✓ | `ops.message-not-confirmation` A message doesn't confirm an operation, whatever it says; the Personal Agent confirms only at the operations endpoint. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L39) | MUST | both | `conv/operation-message` |
| ✓ | `ops.website-same-operation` Confirming an operation on the website and at the endpoint can't perform it twice. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L40) | MUST | company | `ops/website-confirm` |

## Operations 5.1 Getting the User's approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ops.approval` Before confirming, the Personal Agent has the User's approval for the revision, by the User (`approved_by: "user"`) or by a standing permission, which is not allowed when `user_approval_required` is true. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L44) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.show-summary` The Personal Agent shows the User the Company's name and the revision's `summary`, and takes the User's answer through its own interface. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L45) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.company-text-not-approval` The Personal Agent does not treat text from the Company, such as a conversation message, as the User's approval. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L46) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.standing-permission` A standing permission covers the Company, the account, the action and every term of the revision, and is still in effect. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L47) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.approval-per-revision` An approval covers one revision, so a new revision needs a new approval unless a standing permission covers it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L48) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 5.2 Confirming

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.confirm-checks` Before performing the action, the Company checks that the Session Token may use the operation, that it has the needed scopes (`insufficient_scope` or `sign_in_required`), that `revision` is the latest (`terms_changed` with the current operation), and that `approved_by` is allowed (`user_approval_required`). _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L54) | MUST | company | `ops/revisions`<br>`ops/approval` |
| ✓ | `ops.confirm-idempotent` Confirming an operation that is not `proposed` or has expired returns the operation as it is and does nothing else. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L55) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm` |
| ✓ | `ops.confirm-progress` A confirmed operation moves to `in_progress`; the response carries the final state if the action finishes within a few seconds, or `in_progress` with `Retry-After`, and it continues even if the Session Token expires or the User signs out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L56) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm`<br>`ops/in-progress` |

## Operations 6 Tracking and recovery

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.retry-after` While an operation is `in_progress`, the Company includes `Retry-After` when it is read, and the Personal Agent reads again after that time. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L60) | SHOULD | both | `ops/in-progress` |
| ✓ | `ops.at-most-once` The Company performs each operation at most once, however many times and through whichever channels it is confirmed. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L61) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm`<br>`ops/performs`<br>`ops/website-confirm` |
| ✓ | `ops.failed-only-if-known` The Company does not report `failed` while it doesn't know whether the action took effect. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L62) | MUST NOT | company | `ops/unknown-outcome` |
| → | `ops.no-reproposal` After a failed or timed-out confirm, the Personal Agent does not ask for a new proposal of the same action until the operation is final. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L63) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `ops.result-summary` In a final state, `result.summary` describes every change that was made, including any made by an operation that failed or was cancelled partway. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L64) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm` |

## Operations 7 Cancelling

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.cancel` Cancelling makes a `proposed` operation `cancelled`, stops an `in_progress` one if the Company can while it stays `in_progress` until the outcome is known, and returns a final operation as it is. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L68) | MUST | company | `ops/cancel`<br>`ops/in-progress` |

## Operations 8 What a confirmation proves

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `ops.revoke-false-approval` A Company may revoke the `client_id` of a Personal Agent that confirms without the approval it claims. [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L72) | MAY | company |  |

## Operations 9 Errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `ops.errors` The operations endpoint returns JSON errors: `operation_not_found` 404, `terms_changed` 409 with the current operation, `user_approval_required` 403, and `extension_required` 403 from other channels. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.1/ext-operations.md#L76) | MUST | company | `ops/revisions`<br>`ops/approval`<br>`ops/access`<br>`ops/require-extension` |

## Guides: For both parties

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✎ | `guide.secrets` Keep tokens, private keys, assertions, proofs, device codes, one-time codes and mediated credentials out of logs, telemetry, error reports, model context, conversation messages and URLs, redacting the `Authorization`, `DPoP` and `Cookie` headers before logging. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L7) | SHOULD | both | _Poppyseed never logs tokens or request bodies; review with each change to logging_ |
| ✓ | `guide.no-store` Send `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response that carries a token or code. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L8) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/token-response-not-cached` |
| ✓ | `guide.algorithms` Support ES256 and RS256, sign with ES256 when you can, use RSA keys of at least 2048 bits, and reject `alg: none` and symmetric algorithms such as HS256. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L9) | SHOULD | both | `guide/jwt-algorithms` |
| ✓ | `guide.assertion-keys` Verify assertions only with keys from the Personal Agent's verified `jwks_uri`, ignoring `jku`, `x5u` and any key embedded in an assertion. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L10) | SHOULD | company | `identity/assertion-lifetime` |
| ✓ | `guide.assertion-time` Check `aud`, `exp` and `iat`, allow a small clock skew such as 30 seconds, and reject assertions that claim a long lifetime. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L11) | SHOULD | company | `identity/assertion-lifetime`<br>`identity/assertion-fresh` |
| ✓ | `guide.jti-entropy` Make each `jti` at least 128 random bits. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L12) | SHOULD | both | `guide/jti-entropy`<br>`dpop/jti-entropy` |
| → | `guide.key-rotation` Give every key a `kid`, publish a new key before signing with it, and keep an old public key published until everything signed with it has expired. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L13) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `guide.refetch-on-unknown-kid` Refetch `jwks_uri` when an unknown `kid` appears, with a rate limit so a stream of bad assertions can't trigger a fetch each time. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L14) | SHOULD | company | `identity/metadata-fetch-bounded` |
| ✎ | `guide.fetch-limits` Limit metadata fetches to a few redirects, a response size such as 100 KB, and a timeout of a few seconds, and validate HTTPS certificates. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L15) | SHOULD | both | _redirects are not followed, bodies over 100 KB are cut off, fetches time out after 5 s; covered by core review_ |
| ✓ | `guide.metadata-no-credentials` Never send cookies, tokens or other credentials on metadata fetches. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L16) | SHOULD | both | `guide/metadata-fetch-credentials` |
| ✓ | `guide.private-addresses` Reject loopback, private and link-local addresses unless configured on purpose, checking the address actually connected to. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L17) | SHOULD | both | `identity/private-agent-urls`<br>_on Node the metadata fetch checks the address it connects to (packages/core/src/safe-fetch.ts); core unit test packages/core/test/safe-fetch.test.ts_ |
| ✎ | `guide.cache-bounds` Cache metadata according to HTTP caching headers, within bounds such as at least a minute and at most a day. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L18) | SHOULD | both | _client metadata is cached for its max-age, between a minute and a day; core unit test packages/core/test/client-cache.test.ts_ |
| ✓ | `guide.idempotency-key` Send an `Idempotency-Key` (a random UUID v4) on API writes that accept one, and as a Company keep idempotency records per session for a set time, returning the original response for a repeated key and rejecting a repeated key with a different body. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L19) | SHOULD | both | `guide/idempotency-key` |
| ✓ | `guide.retries` Each retry needs a new DPoP Proof and a retried token request needs a new assertion; wait at least `Retry-After` on 429 or 503, and otherwise back off exponentially with jitter. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L20) | SHOULD | both | `ops/in-progress` |
| ✓ | `guide.rate-limits` Limit by `client_id`, by User and by Session, and send the `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L21) | SHOULD | company | `tokens/rate-limit` |
| ✓ | `guide.json` Use TLS 1.2 or later, encode JSON as UTF-8, reject objects with duplicate member names, write timestamps in RFC 3339 with an offset, and ignore unrecognized fields. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L22) | SHOULD | both | `guide/json` |

## Guides: For personal agents

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.user-ids` Make User IDs random per User and Company, or derive them with a keyed hash of a random internal ID and the Company's `auth.issuer`. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L26) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.dpop-keys` Generate a non-extractable DPoP key pair per User per Company, keep private keys away from models and their tools, sign proofs where the final method and URL are known, and never follow redirects with an old proof. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L27) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.token-storage` Encrypt Account Tokens at rest away from the model, keep Session Tokens in memory, request Bearer tokens only for MCP, and delete an Account Token on `invalid_grant`. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L28) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.sign-in-choice` Prefer direct, then device, then Mediated Sign-In, and ask for the fewest scopes the task needs. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L29) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.direct-device` Open the authorization URL in the User's own browser, make `state` random and single-use, poll no faster than `interval`, and add 5 seconds on `slow_down`. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L30) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.agent-mediated` Collect mediated fields outside the model and discard credentials once an Account Token exists. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L31) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.distributed-apps` Keep the signing private key on a server, not in a distributed app. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L32) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.browsing` Use a separate browser storage context per Session, never type the User's credentials into a website, and close the context when the Session ends. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L33) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.agent-conversations` Read events with a long wait or a stream, summarize before a handoff, and close conversations when the task is done. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L34) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.interfaces` Prefer a Company's APIs and Company Agent over browsing, and don't phone a Company that publishes a `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L35) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: For companies

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `guide.client-fetch` Fetch the `client_id` URL without following redirects, cache client metadata and key sets, keep allowlists or blocklists, and rate-limit Session creation and new `client_id` values. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L39) | SHOULD | company | `guide/client-fetch` |
| ✓ | `guide.dpop-header` Check that a proof's `typ` is `dpop+jwt`, its `alg` is allowed, and its `jwk` holds only a public key. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L40) | SHOULD | company | `dpop/signature` |
| ✎ | `guide.replay-cache` Keep one replay cache shared by every server, keyed by `jti` for the acceptance window. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L41) | SHOULD | company | _jti replay records live in the configured Store, which postgresStore() shares across instances_ |
| ✎ | `guide.public-htu` Compare `htu` with the public URL the Personal Agent used, built from the configured public origin rather than the received `Host` header. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L42) | SHOULD | company | _htu is built from the configured baseUrl; pnpm e2e exercises it through Next.js rewrites_ |
| ✎ | `guide.dpop-window` Use an acceptance window of about one minute plus a small clock skew. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L43) | SHOULD | company | _the window is 90 seconds, set in packages/core/src/dpop.ts_ |
| ✎ | `guide.conversation-endpoint-only` Serve Personal Agent conversations only from the conversation endpoint. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L44) | SHOULD | company | _Poppyseed serves conversations only at the conversation endpoint, behind DPoP; keep website chat on its own records_ |
| ✓ | `guide.token-lifetimes` Give Account Tokens a lifetime that fits the account, such as 90 days, expire unused ones sooner, and revoke them on a password reset or suspected compromise. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L45) | SHOULD | company | `account/refresh` |
| ✓ | `guide.consent-page` On the consent page, show the Personal Agent's name, logo and `client_id` domain, the account, each scope in plain language and how long access lasts; protect it against CSRF and framing; accept only PKCE S256; and return `iss` in every redirect. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L46) | SHOULD | company | `direct/consent-page` |
| ✓ | `guide.device` Ask the User to confirm the code matches, return `slow_down` to fast pollers, limit wrong `user_code` entries, and keep `expires_in` short, such as 10 minutes. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L47) | SHOULD | company | `device/abuse` |
| ✓ | `guide.company-mediated` Rate-limit Mediated Sign-In by account, `client_id` and User ID, cap wrong codes, return the same failure for an unknown account and a wrong password, never store raw credentials, and tell the User when a Personal Agent signs in. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L48) | SHOULD | company | `mediated/failures` |
| ✓ | `guide.account-settings` List each connected Personal Agent with its name, domain, scopes and last use, with a control to disconnect it. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L49) | SHOULD | company | `signout/disconnect` |
| ✓ | `guide.browser-sessions` Don't log request bodies at the browser session endpoint, limit the cookie to the hosts Personal Agents need, and look up the Session on each request. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L50) | SHOULD | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✓ | `guide.scopes-everywhere` Apply the same scope rules on the website, APIs, Company Agent and live agents through one shared check, and check `poppy:read` and `poppy:write` separately. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L51) | SHOULD | company | `signin/partial-approval` |
| ✎ | `guide.internal-services` Verify the Session Token at the edge and pass the verified `client_id`, User ID, account and scopes to internal services, never the token itself. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L52) | SHOULD | company | _the tool context carries the verified identity, never the token_ |
| ✎ | `guide.guest-access` Let a signed-out Session do what a signed-out visitor can do, and limit abuse with rate limits by `client_id` rather than by turning Personal Agents away. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L53) | SHOULD | company | _a policy each Company sets with its tools' scopes_ |
| ✓ | `guide.company-conversations` Keep a conversation's events for at least 30 days, send an SSE comment every 15 to 30 seconds on an idle stream, close account conversations when a Session signs out, and say so before closing an inactive conversation. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L54) | SHOULD | company | `conv/account-bound` |
| ✓ | `guide.error-messages` Keep error text free of account details and other users' data, and return the same error for "doesn't exist" and "belongs to someone else". [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L55) | SHOULD | company | `guide/same-error` |

## Guides: For the Operations extension

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.ops-agents` Show the summary as the Company wrote it with the Company and account, show what changed in a new revision, store standing permissions with their limits and check each against the terms, reserve limited uses before confirming, and after a timeout read or confirm again with the same revision. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L59) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `guide.ops-downstream` Derive downstream idempotency keys from the operation ID, and after a downstream timeout ask that system whether the action happened before retrying, keeping the operation `in_progress` until known. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L60) | SHOULD | company | `ops/unknown-outcome` |
| ✓ | `guide.ops-dedupe` Before proposing, look for an open operation in the same Session or account with the same terms. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L61) | SHOULD | company | `ops/dedupe` |
| ✎ | `guide.ops-retention` Keep final operations readable as long as the User can see the related order or booking, or at least 30 days. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L62) | SHOULD | company | _operations are kept for a year (RETAIN_MS in packages/core/src/operations.ts); not observable in a test run_ |
| ✎ | `guide.ops-summary` Write the summary so it stands alone: what will happen, to what, and any cost, date or condition. [↗](pap-0.1/guides.md#L63) | SHOULD | company | _written by the Company's own handlers_ |
